rows.description: City Commission (Nov 23): purchase of 515 Visa gift cards from Corporate Traditions, Inc. for distribution to the city's regular full-time and part-time employees during the holiday season, $52,812.50 (0.15% of general fund). Vote pending.

Nov 17 (WCTV): Commissioner Fred Nicholas II: "They want a tax cut; they want us to tighten our belts." County projects about $5M less revenue in FY2027-28 and another $1M the next year; senior council and other outside funding approved for two quarters pending a budget workshop.

Nov 19 (Suncoast Searchlight): Chairman Tal Siddique: "Building new parks, new libraries, extensions, all that needs to just stop." Staff estimate $63M less in year one, $113M in year two; $2B five-year CIP to be paused and reconsidered.

Nov 18 (The Center Square): Commissioner Mark Smith: "This SAFER grant buys us some time" ($7.6M federal grant for 25 firefighters). Administrator Jonathan Lewis says funded groups were warned money "may not be there October of next year."

Nov 19 (Florida Daily): PSTA CEO Brad Miller says PSTA's board faces the "same difficult decisions" after Amendment 3; up to 25 of 40 routes could be eliminated; projected shortfall approaching $34M. Pairs with St. Pete Beach ending its trolley funding.

WFTV, Nov 19: "Florida auditors question over $1.5 million in Daytona Beach permit fund expenses". Preliminary Auditor General findings: $480,376 in non-allowable permit fund charges (City Hall AV upgrades, charity golf sponsorships), $1,050,979 in wages; $775 commissioner p-card meal.

rows.government: Pinellas Suncoast Transit Authority / St. Pete Beach
rows.description: Florida Daily, Nov 19: "Amendment 3 Prompts Pinellas County Officials to Cut Several Public Transportation Services". St. Pete Beach ends $242,000 FY2027 trolley funding; PSTA projects a shortfall approaching $34M.
rows.shortfall: PSTA: projected shortfall approaching $34M; up to 25 of 40 routes at risk (Nov 19, 2026)
